back2basics.concept: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT)
back2basics.text: AML/CFT refers to laws, regulations, and procedures designed to prevent criminals from disguising illegally obtained funds as legitimate income and to stop the financing of terrorism. Financial institutions and intermediaries must monitor transactions, conduct customer due diligence, and report suspicious activities to regulatory authorities to maintain financial system integrity.

This aims to enhance their expertise in identifying suspicious transactions and complying with AML/CFT regulations, which is crucial for maintaining market integrity.

body.label: Mandatory certification
body.text: SEBI proposes that principal officers of all registered intermediaries must obtain AML/CFT certification to ensure they have adequate expertise in anti-money laundering and counter-terror financing measures.

body.label: Certification scope
body.text: The certification covers knowledge of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, customer due diligence, beneficial ownership, risk-based client classification, enhanced due diligence, transaction monitoring, targeted financial sanctions, reporting obligations, and emerging risks from new products and technologies.

body.label: Compliance timeline
body.text: Both existing and newly appointed principal officers would have six months to comply with the certification requirement.

sections.heading: What is SEBI's new proposal on AML/CFT certification?

body.label: Ensuring expertise
body.text: Principal officers play a central role in identifying suspicious transactions, assessing money laundering risks, and reporting to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India, so SEBI wants to standardize their knowledge and competence.

body.label: Current gaps
body.text: Currently, there is no specific AML/CFT certification requirement, leading to varying levels of expertise among principal officers across intermediaries.

sections.heading: Why does SEBI want mandatory AML/CFT certification?

body.label: Collaboration with NISM
body.text: SEBI has collaborated with the National Institute of Securities Markets (NISM) to develop a certification examination covering AML/CFT provisions in the securities market.

body.label: Existing certification
body.text: NISM launched the Series-XXIV AML/CFT certification examination in February 2025, which will be used for this purpose.

body.label: Consultation process
body.text: SEBI has invited public comments on the proposal until November 27, 2026.

back2basics.text: The northeast monsoon is a critical rainfall period for Tamil Nadu, supplying most of the state's annual precipitation. Reservoirs store this water to support agriculture and drinking needs during dry periods. Water management involves balancing reservoir releases and inter-state river water sharing to sustain farming and avoid shortages.

back2basics.text: Treasury Bills are short-term debt instruments issued by the government to meet temporary funding needs. body.text: Automation is often feared to cause job losses, especially for low-skilled workers, but ABB India's experience shows it can increase employment and inclusivity.

body.label: Skill development
